title: PPO on LunarLander (small budget)
paper: Schulman et al. 2017, Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
claim: PPO learns a harder control task, and the from-scratch version matches the library.
setup: LunarLander-v3, only 100000 steps, 3 seeds, same hyper-parameters for SB3 and scratch PPO. Return of 200 counts as solved; that normally needs several times this budget.
result: SB3 -340.3 ± 102.4; scratch -357.4 ± 299.8 (greedy eval over 10 episodes). Difference 17.1; neither reaches 200.
verdict_reason: Implementations are within noise of each other (rule: gap <= max(2 std, 20)); verdict is 'not reproduced' unless both reach 200, because the claim includes actually learning the task.
mismatches: The step budget is far below what PPO needs to solve LunarLander, so this tests parity, not final performance.
Only 3 seeds, and no hyper-parameter tuning.
